drought: The earth will open its mouth and drink only dust; the ears of grain will bow beneath a brazen sky.
Helios will linger over the furrows, and the spring will fall silent before the grain ripens.
The clouds will pass without stopping, and the wheat will thirst in its husk.
good_year: The branches will bend beneath their burden, and the press will sing longer than is its wont.
The boughs of Athena and the vines of Dionysos will bear more than they promise.
Let the baskets be ready: the sap is rising, and the fruit will come in crowds.
storm: Poseidon will strike the sea with his trident; the prudent sailor will wait in port until the foam settles.
The winds of Aeolus will quarrel over the road of the ships, and the voyage will grow long.
The sky will split above the waves; what sets out will be late to arrive, but it will arrive.
caravan: Camels will come from the East, and their masters will have but one word on their lips: {{good}}.
The stranger will knock at the gates of the agora; what he desires has a name: {{good}}.
A distant dust heralds full purses; they will open for this: {{good}}.
